subject: Sliding versus hinged wardrobe doors
hook: My floor is not level. Can I still have sliding wardrobe doors?
fb:
One of the questions we get most from people in older houses: 'Our bedroom floor is not level. Can we still have sliding wardrobe doors?'

Usually, yes. Sliding doors depend on level tracks rather than a level floor, so the floor and ceiling are checked at the survey, and the tracks are set level when we fit. Uneven walls are dealt with using scribed fillers, cut to follow the line of the wall.

If your floor has a serious slope, mention it at the consultation, as it can change which doors we would suggest. Ask your question or arrange a visit here:
https://superiofurniture.com/contact/?utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=autumn-interiors-and-practical-comfort&utm_content=day-070
gbp:
Will sliding wardrobe doors work if my floor is not level?

In most homes, yes. Sliding doors depend on level tracks rather than a perfectly level floor. At the survey we check the floor and ceiling, and on fitting day our own team sets the top and bottom tracks level and adjusts each door so it runs smoothly and meets evenly.

Walls that are out of true are handled with scribed fillers, cut to follow the wall so there are no gaps along the edge. Sloping ceilings can be built around too, although they sometimes make hinged doors the more practical choice.

If your bedroom floor has a noticeable slope, it is worth mentioning at the free, no-obligation design consultation so we can talk through the options. SUPERIO fitted wardrobes are made in our Hanley workshop and fitted across Stoke-on-Trent and Staffordshire.
